candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — cleaning/disinfection and prevention of transmission
candidate.educational_objective: Apply CDC cleaning and disinfection recommendations for shared noncritical patient-care equipment.

options.A: Share them without cleaning when clients have no visible infection.
options.B: Clean them only on a weekly schedule regardless of use.
options.C: Clean and disinfect the shared equipment before and after each patient use according to facility and manufacturer-compatible procedures.
options.D: Avoid disinfection because noncritical equipment cannot transmit pathogens.

candidate.rationale: CDC identifies blood pressure cuffs and stethoscopes as shared noncritical patient-care equipment. Current environmental-cleaning guidance recommends cleaning and disinfecting shared equipment before and after each use. Therefore C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Shared noncritical equipment such as blood pressure cuffs and stethoscopes should be cleaned and disinfected before and after each patient use using compatible products/procedures.
candidate.source_document_title: Environmental Cleaning Procedures — Noncritical Patient Care Equipment
candidate.source_locator: Section 4.7 Noncritical patient care equipment; Table 26 — Shared equipment: before and after each use, clean and disinfect
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A reusable blood pressure cuff and stethoscope are shared among clients on an inpatient unit. What is the appropriate infection-prevention practice?
